# Introduction

This assignment corresponds to Weeks 4-5 of the course, "Unsupervised Learning," and focuses on Principal Component Analysis (PCA). You will reuse the tract-level SoVI data from HW_01 (no new data pipeline work is required) to explore how PCA summarizes a large set of correlated social-vulnerability variables into a small number of components, how standardizing variables before fitting PCA changes the result, and how the structure PCA finds can itself vary across different subsets of the data (here, different states).

## Before You Begin

You will fit PCA in several different settings in this assignment. It will be easiest to write a *function* in Python that performs PCA on a given dataset. The function should include an argument that decides how the PCA should be done (e.g., whether to standardize the data first). You may find it useful to write additional functions for plotting PCA results or comparing two PCA results to each other, since you will be making several such comparisons below.
